<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (literal, 42 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 459afea1f69ff69422de2a7a2c7674b6f7ea1aca` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7d8df8e6fe4e442cfe5def08f41efec4e8069eb8` — the merge of head `c8b1dce6365cf61c7d8c95bb44dc08a0edc3fed0` into base `459afea1f69ff69422de2a7a2c7674b6f7ea1aca`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7d8df8e6fe4e442cfe5def08f41efec4e8069eb8 && git checkout 7d8df8e6fe4e442cfe5def08f41efec4e8069eb8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 459afea1f69ff69422de2a7a2c7674b6f7ea1aca c8b1dce6365cf61c7d8c95bb44dc08a0edc3fed0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 459afea1f69ff69422de2a7a2c7674b6f7ea1aca && git merge --no-ff c8b1dce6365cf61c7d8c95bb44dc08a0edc3fed0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 459afea1f69ff69422de2a7a2c7674b6f7ea1aca
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 459afea1f69ff69422de2a7a2c7674b6f7ea1aca` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `629addbf97035ec1330d7fa4c016e5aa556a62c6`
Local-runs: none

The review is owed by the `Clause-②: yes` declaration alone (the claim `6327912966`, the PR body and the changeset). No published schema and no governed path are in the committed tree (8 files: `plugin-auth`, `plugin-email`, `.changeset/`). It was read from the diff, the card, ruling 1B (`6308462370` on #25040) and the seat calls (`6309679111`). ⛔ Disclosure (#9387, `5323310017`): behaviour only.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set change:** the public email-and-password sign-up answers an existing address differently in one configuration. When all three of these hold, the explicit refusal becomes the vendor's generic success, plus a mail to the holder:
  - the posture is `open` or `email_domain`;
  - the vendor's anti-enumeration shield is on (verification required, or auto sign-in off), read from the options the vendor itself reads;
  - `IEmailService.isConfigured()` answers `true`, read per request.

  This matches ruling 1B. **Correct.**
- **The precondition:** a missing member, a throwing member and a `false` answer all keep the refusal (`isEmailDeliveryLive`). `hasEmailTransport` / `isEmailServiceAvailable` are not repurposed. This matches the ruling's "not live ⇒ refusal" and Q1. **Correct.**
- **`invite_only`** is unchanged. **`open` with the shield off** keeps the refusal (Q3, no session for someone else's account). **Correct.**
- **The mail:** the vendor hook re-asks posture and liveness, so the unanswerable-probe fall-through cannot mail under `invite_only`.
  - It skips placeholder addresses.
  - It uses the stored locale, then the deployment default, with no request rung (Q2).
  - It links to the Console's sign-in and forgot-password pages and mints no token.
  - It never throws, and logs a failed send at error level once.

  **Correct.**
- **The after-hook line:** it skips `password_changed_at` for the rowless id of the success answer. The need is measured (pin ①, ablation A7), and the amended claim `6329490109` accepts it. **Correct.**
- **Public surface:** no export is added (`src/index.ts` is untouched). The template is one more row in the existing built-in registry. **No widening beyond the declared door change.**

### ② Semver level

`patch` for `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/plugin-email`, with `Metadata-protocol: none`. This follows #25105's ruling A (closed: minor only when the metadata protocol changes). No authorable key, value or metadata type changes. The card's "minor" predates that ruling. **Consistent.**

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The dev's open question 1** (the docs page made false) is answered A by the amended claim `6329490109`: a patch round corrects that one section of `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`, a prose face this record does not gate.
- **The missing `src/index.ts` re-export** stays an Acceptance note: nothing this PR touched becomes false.
- **The out-of-scope reading** (the pre-existing stamp warning on the probe-failure path) is carried as an Acceptance note: carrier none, noted, not filed.
- **Ablation A3** (the shield conjunct is defence in depth, backed by the vendor's identical refusal) is recorded in the PR.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-25060-signup-existing-address`
Reviewed-by: `session_01UnHcTADjeg3VwxF21QHj7W`

**VERDICT: PASS**
